title: Why Can't Cells Get Any Bigger?

1.title: The problem: why cells stay small

q.1(b): 1(b). Name one substance that enters a cell by diffusion and one that leaves it by diffusion.
q.1(c): 1(c). A cube of side 2 cm has a surface area of 24 cm² and a volume of 8 cm³. Calculate its surface area to volume ratio.

q.2(a): 2(a). Write a hypothesis. Predict which cube will take the longest to turn completely colourless, and give a reason using the words surface area and volume.
q.2(c): 2(c). Write a method of 5 numbered steps that another Grade 9 class could follow exactly.

3.title: Watch the practical and record the results

q.Table: 3(a). The class's shared times: how long did each cube take to turn completely colourless?
q.3(b): 3(b). State one reason why the times in the video might not be exactly reproduced if you ran this practical yourselves.

4.title: Ratios, the graph and the pattern

q.Table: 4(a). Complete the table: surface area, volume and ratio for each cube.
q.4(c): 4(c). Describe the pattern your graph shows.

q.5(a): 5(a). Write a conclusion that answers the research question, and use it to explain why real cells stay small.
q.5(b): 5(b). You only watched three cubes. State one reason why this weakens the conclusion.
q.5(c): 5(c). An agar cube is a model of a cell, not a real cell. State one important way a real cell is different.

q.Predictions revisited: Look back at your hypothesis in 2(a). Did the results support it? Explain in one sentence.
q.Revision plan: Anything not ticked is your revision list. Which will you revise first, and how?
q.Question: One question you still have

obj: Explain why the surface area to volume ratio, not size alone, limits how big a cell can be.
Plan an investigation yourself: hypothesis, variables and a method another class could follow (Criterion B).
Calculate surface area to volume ratios, draw a graph and describe the pattern (Criterion C).
Write a conclusion, link it to real cells, and evaluate the evidence and the model (Criterion C).
